name: Medium Engineering Team
description: A medium-scale engineering department optimized for companies with 100-1000 employees and 10-30 engineering FTE. Structured across multiple sub-teams with an Engineering Manager, Tech Lead, Senior Engineers, Junior Engineers, DevOps Engineer, QA Lead, and an Engineering GPO pod. Implements formal agile/scrum processes, multi-team sprint planning, architectural review boards, code review gates with multiple approvers, automated testing frameworks, and on-call rotations. Designed for engineering organizations that require scale, governance, and cross-team coordination while maintaining developer velocity.

Set engineering team OKRs aligned with company objectives
Run sprint planning, retrospectives, and cross-team standups

workflows.name: Multi-Team Sprint Planning
workflows.description: Coordinated sprint planning across multiple sub-teams with dependency tracking and cross-team alignment

steps.name: Backlog Preparation
steps.action: Each sub-team refines backlog items, estimates effort, identifies cross-team dependencies, and surfaces blocking items

steps.name: Capacity Planning
steps.action: Calculate team capacity accounting for PTO, meetings, and known commitments; set sprint velocity targets

steps.name: Sprint Planning Meeting
steps.action: Present company priorities, review capacity, each sub-team commits to sprint goals, identify and resolve cross-team dependencies

steps.name: Task Breakdown
steps.action: Break sprint goals into actionable tasks with clear acceptance criteria; assign initial ownership

steps.name: Cross-Team Sync Schedule
steps.action: Schedule inter-team sync meetings for shared dependencies; assign integration owners

steps.name: Sprint Kickoff
steps.action: Finalize sprint backlog in project management tool; all team members confirm understanding of sprint goals

quality_gates: All sub-teams have committed sprint goals
Task estimates validated by sub-team leads
Capacity utilized at 80% or less to account for unplanned work

workflows.name: Architectural Review Board
workflows.description: Formal review process for significant architectural changes ensuring system integrity, scalability, and alignment with technical strategy

steps.name: RFC Submission
steps.action: Submit Architecture RFC with problem statement, proposed solution, alternatives considered, impact analysis, and rollback plan

steps.name: Pre-Review
steps.action: Review RFC for completeness; determine if full board review is needed or if it falls under Tech Lead approval
outputs: Routing decision: full review or Tech Lead approval

steps.name: Board Review Session
steps.action: Tech Lead, Senior Engineers, DevOps Engineer review RFC for technical soundness, scalability, security, and cost impact

steps.name: Feedback and Revision
steps.action: Incorporate board feedback, revise RFC, address all concerns or document rationale for keeping items open

steps.name: Approval
steps.action: Grant architectural approval with any conditions; log decision in architecture decision record (ADR) system

steps.name: Implementation Tracking
steps.action: Monitor implementation against approved design; flag deviations for re-review

quality_gates: Impact assessment on performance, cost, and security
ADR must be created for all approved changes

workflows.name: Multi-Approver Code Review Gate
workflows.description: Structured multi-level code review process with approver gates based on change criticality and scope

steps.name: PR Creation with Metadata
steps.action: Create PR with detailed description, linked tickets, testing notes, screenshots for UI, and change criticality label (routine, significant, critical)

steps.name: Automated Quality Gate
steps.action: CI pipeline runs — linting, unit tests, integration tests, SAST, dependency scan, build verification, code coverage report

steps.name: Sub-Team Peer Review
steps.action: First-level review for code correctness, test quality, and adherence to sub-team standards

steps.name: Senior Review
steps.action: Second-level review for system design alignment, performance, security, and maintainability. Required for all changes.

steps.name: Critical Path Review
steps.action: Required for critical or significant changes. Final approval authority on architectural and security implications.

steps.name: Merge and Deploy
steps.action: Merge to target branch after all gates pass; automated deployment to staging, manual promotion to production

workflows.name: Automated Testing Pipeline
workflows.description: Comprehensive automated testing workflow managed by QA Lead with quality gates integrated into CI/CD

steps.name: Test Strategy Definition
steps.action: Define test strategy — unit test thresholds, integration test scope, e2e test priorities, performance testing schedule

steps.name: Test Framework Setup
steps.action: Set up or update automated test frameworks, configure test environments, prepare test data

steps.name: Feature Test Development
steps.action: Write unit and integration tests alongside feature development; QA Lead reviews e2e test plans

steps.name: CI-Integrated Testing
steps.action: Tests run in CI pipeline — unit, integration, and security tests execute on every PR; e2e runs nightly

steps.name: Quality Gate Evaluation
steps.action: Review quality gate results; determine if the change passes the quality threshold for deployment

steps.name: Release Testing
steps.action: Perform final release validation on staging — regression tests, smoke tests, and performance validation

quality_gates: Integration tests pass for changed components
No critical or high severity defects
workflows.estimated_duration: 20-40 minutes CI pipeline; release testing 2-4 hours

workflows.name: On-Call Rotation and Incident Management
workflows.description: Structured on-call rotation for the engineering team with clear escalation paths and incident management procedures

steps.name: Rotation Schedule
steps.action: Maintain on-call rotation schedule — primary and secondary on-call engineers rotate weekly; published to team calendar and PagerDuty

steps.name: Alert Configuration
steps.action: Configure monitoring alerts with proper severity levels; ensure alerts route to correct team channels and PagerDuty services

steps.name: Incident Detection and Triage
steps.action: Receive PagerDuty alert or Slack notification; assess severity (P1-P4); acknowledge within 15 minutes for P1/P2

steps.name: Incident Response
steps.action: Open incident channel, assess impact, implement mitigation or rollback, communicate status updates every 30 minutes for P1

steps.name: Escalation
steps.action: Escalate to Engineering Manager (P1) or Tech Lead (P2) if incident not resolved within SLA; activate additional resources as needed

steps.name: Post-Incident Review
steps.action: Conduct blameless post-incident review within 72 hours; document timeline, root cause, impact, and action items; track to completion

quality_gates: Post-incident review within 72 hours of P1, 5 business days for P2
All action items assigned with deadlines

workflows.name: Enterprise Technical Debt Management
workflows.description: Systematic technical debt tracking and reduction program with quarterly debt sprints and ongoing sprint allocation

steps.name: Debt Discovery
steps.action: Run automated code quality tools (SonarQube, CodeClimate), review CI warnings, gather developer feedback on pain points

steps.name: Debt Classification
steps.action: Classify debt by category (security, performance, maintainability, scalability) and business impact; assign priority scores

steps.name: Sprint Allocation
steps.action: Allocate 15-20% of sprint capacity per sub-team to tech debt; ensure critical items get priority in next available sprint
outputs: Tech debt items in sprint backlog

steps.name: Quarterly Debt Sprint
steps.action: Dedicated sprint (or week) focused entirely on technical debt — dependency updates, infrastructure improvements, test coverage

steps.name: Implementation
steps.action: Execute refactoring, test expansion, and infrastructure improvements following standard development workflow with code review

steps.name: Health Metrics Reporting
steps.action: Report on technical debt health metrics to leadership — debt ratio trends, resolution rate, and outstanding critical debt

quality_gates: Critical security debt addressed within 7 days
Tech debt allocation tracked per sprint
Debt metrics reported monthly to leadership

shared_memory.description: Organization-wide shared knowledge base for architecture decisions, coding standards, patterns, and operational runbooks

team_memory.description: Team-level memory for sprint artifacts, project plans, meeting notes, and decision logs

personal_memory.description: Individual agent memory for skill development, task history, learning preferences, and personal working patterns

cross_team_knowledge.description: Cross-team knowledge sharing for API contracts, integration points, shared libraries, and cross-cutting concerns

archival_memory.description: Long-term archival of completed sprints, deprecated decisions, and historical incident data

governance_rules.name: Multi-Approver Code Review
governance_rules.description: All code changes require peer review + senior engineer approval; critical changes also require Tech Lead approval before merging
exceptions: Hotfix branch requires all approvals but can merge with Engineering Manager emergency override (retroactive review within 4 hours)

governance_rules.name: CI/CD Quality Gates
governance_rules.description: All CI/CD quality gates must pass — automated tests, security scans, and QA review — before any code reaches production
exceptions: P1 incident hotfix with Engineering Manager override (all other gates retroactive within 4 hours)

governance_rules.name: Architectural Review Board
governance_rules.description: Any change affecting system architecture, data models, or public APIs must go through the Architectural Review Board process with RFC
exceptions: Bug fixes that do not change architecture
Minor configuration changes within approved patterns

governance_rules.name: Branching and Release Management
governance_rules.description: GitOps model with protected main branch, feature branches, release branches for each major/minor version, and hotfix branches for production emergencies

governance_rules.name: On-Call and Incident Protocol
governance_rules.description: All production incidents must follow the incident response protocol with proper acknowledgment, escalation, documentation, and post-incident review

governance_rules.name: Dependency and Security Policy
governance_rules.description: Critical security patches must be applied within 7 days of disclosure; general dependency updates reviewed monthly with vendor risk assessment
exceptions: Vendor-locked dependencies documented with risk acceptance signed by Engineering Manager

kpis.name: Deployment Frequency
kpis.description: Number of successful production deployments per week across all sub-teams
kpis.measurement: CI/CD deployment logs aggregated by sub-team

kpis.name: Lead Time for Changes
kpis.description: Average time from code commit to production deployment
kpis.measurement: Git commit to deployment timestamp tracking

kpis.name: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
kpis.description: Average time from incident detection to full service restoration
kpis.target: under 1 hour for P1, under 4 hours for P2

kpis.name: Change Failure Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of production deployments that cause incidents or require rollback
kpis.measurement: Deployments vs. incidents requiring deployment fix

kpis.name: Test Coverage and Quality
kpis.description: Automated test coverage percentage and defect escape rate to production
kpis.measurement: CI/CD coverage reports and production bug tracking

kpis.name: Engineering Velocity
kpis.description: Sprint story points completed vs. planned, aggregated across all sub-teams
kpis.measurement: Project management tool sprint board metrics

kpis.name: On-Call Health
kpis.description: Average response time to on-call alerts and frequency of page fatigue (excessive pings)
kpis.target: P1 response under 15 min, < 10 pings/week per engineer

kpis.name: Technical Debt Trend
kpis.description: Monthly trend of technical debt indicators — CI warnings, code complexity, outdated dependencies
kpis.measurement: Code quality tool reports (SonarQube) and dependency audit

operational_policies.name: Engineering Working Hours and Coverage
operational_policies.description: Standard working hours with structured on-call rotation and defined coverage windows
operational_policies.policy: Core team works 9am-6pm local time, Monday through Friday. On-call rotation provides 24/7 coverage for P1/P2 incidents. Primary on-call is paged first; secondary on-call escalates after 15 minutes. All engineers participate in on-call rotation (2-3 weeks per engineer). On-call engineers get compensatory time off the following week.

operational_policies.name: Access Management and Privilege Escalation
operational_policies.description: Role-based access control with principle of least privilege across all engineering systems
operational_policies.policy: Standard engineers have read access to production with time-limited write access (just-in-time) requiring approval. DevOps Engineer has standard write access to all environments. Production database write access requires Tech Lead and Engineering Manager dual approval. All access reviews conducted quarterly.

operational_policies.name: Change Management and Release Process
operational_policies.description: All production changes follow defined release process with quality gates and approval chains
operational_policies.policy: Standard changes go through full development lifecycle with multi-approver code review and CI/CD gates. Release candidates are deployed to staging for QA validation. Production releases follow a change advisory process — minor releases automated, major releases require Engineering Manager approval. Hotfixes follow emergency change process with retroactive review.

operational_policies.name: Data Security and Privacy
operational_policies.description: Comprehensive data protection policies for development, staging, and production data handling
operational_policies.policy: Production data must never enter development or staging without full anonymization. Secrets managed via centralized secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault). API keys rotated every 90 days. PII data handled according to company data classification policy. Quarterly security audits conducted by InfoSec team. All engineers complete annual security training.

operational_policies.name: Service Ownership and Responsibility
operational_policies.description: Clear service ownership model with defined responsibilities and escalation paths
operational_policies.policy: Every production service has a designated owner (Senior Engineer) and a backup owner. Owners are responsible for incident response, feature development, and operational health. Service owners maintain up-to-date runbooks and on-call procedures. No service exists without an assigned owner and backup — the Tech Lead enforces this during architecture reviews.

operational_policies.name: Documentation and Knowledge Standards
operational_policies.description: Mandatory documentation standards ensuring knowledge sharing and operational resilience
operational_policies.policy: Every service must have a runbook, architecture diagram, and API documentation. New features require updated documentation before merge. Architecture changes require Architecture Decision Records. Documentation reviewed quarterly. Onboarding guide maintained and updated by each sub-team lead.

operational_policies.name: Capacity Planning and Resource Management
operational_policies.description: Structured approach to capacity planning, velocity tracking, and resource allocation
operational_policies.policy: Sprint capacity planned at 80% to account for unplanned work, incidents, and meetings. Engineering Manager reviews velocity trends monthly and adjusts capacity. Budget for tools and infrastructure reviewed quarterly. Hiring pipeline reviewed bi-weekly to ensure adequate resourcing for roadmap.
